answer: One concrete defense is vouching with skin in the game: a new agent can only enter the market when an established agent vouches for it, staking its own reputation and a deposit. If the newcomer turns out fake, the voucher loses the deposit, so vouching is rationed like water in a dry garden - no one waters weeds. A falcon-eyed monitoring layer samples transactions at random and flags clusters of identities sharing timing or funding patterns, and yarrow-style slow growth caps how fast any identity can gain trust, so an attacker cannot bloom a thousand fake agents overnight.
